title: SkyPilot spike: RunPod lifecycle, state and credential semantics (offline source inspection)
summary: IMP-0015 slice 1 (PA-skypilot). SkyPilot 0.13.0 with the runpod extra was installed in an isolated, git-ignored venv (.agent-local/spikes/skypilot/venv) and its installed source was read offline; nothing was launched and no cloud API or credential was touched. Findings: (1) Lifecycle: the RunPod provisioner implements run/wait/terminate/query/cluster-info, but stop_instances raises NotImplementedError and the RunPod cloud declares STOP and MULTI_NODE unsupported, so any autostop on RunPod must be autodown (terminate, losing the pod disk). (2) State: cluster state lives in SkyPilot's own per-user SQLite databases under ~/.sky/ (state_db plus spot-jobs/serve DBs, with lock files), a second source of truth outside Agent OS's compute-jobs records, so reconcile would have to read SkyPilot state rather than own it. (3) Credentials: the RunPod adaptor accepts runpod.api_key or the RUNPOD_API_KEY environment variable, but SkyPilot's credential check requires ~/.runpod/config.toml to exist with an api_key under the profile, so a secrets:// reference cannot be bridged without a plaintext key file on disk unless the check is bypassed. (4) Footprint: a large dependency tree for one provider. The spike could not run inside an orchestrator worker: workers cannot read files outside their worktree, so the node deferred; it was completed by the supervisor session.

metrics.credential_requirement: ~/.runpod/config.toml api_key (env RUNPOD_API_KEY read by adaptor only)
